content.title: About
content.content: Dark green vegetables such as spinach, broccoli, kale and collard greens are often used as an ingredient in omelets. They give the dish a vivid color, rich flavor and boost its nutritional value thanks to high levels of vitamins, minerals and fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dark‑green leafy vegetables are rich in chlorophyll, which has antioxidant properties.
Spinach contains more iron than beef, and its plant‑based iron is better absorbed when paired with vitamin C.
Broccoli provides sulforaphane, a compound studied for its potential anti‑cancer effects.
Kale is considered one of the most nutrient‑dense vegetables, offering over 200 % of the daily value of vitamin K per 100 g.
These vegetables can be used as natural food coloring in culinary applications.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Includes folate (B9), essential for DNA synthesis and anemia prevention.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Enhances iron absorption from plant foods and supports immune function.

items.title: Excellent source of vitamin K
items.content: Important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: Calcium, magnesium and potassium support heart, muscle and nerve function.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar and promotes satiety.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Some dark greens (e.g., spinach) contain oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables like broccoli can cause gas when eaten in large amounts.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rare, but possible allergies to specific leafy greens may occur.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add dark green vegetables to an omelet either raw or lightly sautéed first. Chop them finely so they distribute evenly in the egg mixture. Pair with a modest amount of cheese and herbs to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the vegetables in the refrigerator’s crisper drawer, stored in a perforated bag. Use within 3–5 days. For freezing, blanch briefly before packing to preserve color and nutrients.
